# NOTES: TWO BOOKS

## BOOK 1: OUT OF THE BLUE (Bertrand W. Sinclair)

**Core cast:** Rock Holloway (young Texan rider; sorrel horse **Sangre**; black pony carries bed; father Steve Holloway, ex-US marshal at Abilene; uncle Tom "Long Tom" Holloway, Texas Ranger captain; cousin Ben Holloway, Ragged H on Milk River; mother; sister **Cecilia**, 17, marrying a Brett of the B X near El Paso). **Uncle Bill Sayre**, Fort Worth, Trinity Bank president (tall, thin, ~60, Southern dialect). Marcus Proud, Abel Stewart (bank partners). **Dave Snell**, dead Maltese Cross owner (Trinity west fork; ~30,000 cattle moved to Marias, Montana). Heirs: a girl (21, **Alice Snell**) and boy (16). Executors: Sayre and **Buck Walters** (Maltese Cross range boss; flashy, high-handed, fond of women and poker).

**Ch I (Fort Worth):** Rock visits Trinity Bank ("Holy" chalked on door). Sayre talks Seventy Seven trail herd, boss **Elmer Duffy**, brothers **Joe, Ed, Mark** (Mark: big, mean). Sayre hires Rock to watch Buck on Maltese Cross. Gives **$500 gold** in canvas bag as "retaining fee"; $60/month. Rock to report by wire. Rock rides out on sorrel; tells Sangre "we ought to keep time from hanging heavy."

**Ch II (Clark's Ford, Nebraska):** Odeon dance hall/saloon. Rock meets **Al Kerr** (Waco cattleman, gnome-sized, ~5'4", Capital K, Judith Basin on Arrow Creek, post office Lewistown). Mark Duffy, drunk, bullies Kerr, lifts him onto bar, shakes him, fires into floor. Rock intervenes: "Don't be a damn fool." Duffy draws; Rock shoots him dead. Kerr's riders escort them out. Rock rides 3 miles with Kerr; Kerr invites him to Judith Basin. Rock realizes Duffys will seek revenge; Elmer is boss of Seventy Seven.

**Ch III (Steering Wheel):** Rock rides north alone; 3 days out meets Maltese Cross herd (no need to join). Joins short-handed Steering Wheel trail herd (1,200 cattle) at Yellowstone crossing, bound for Fort MacLeod, Canada. Crosses Missouri (Chief Joseph's ford), Bear Paws left, Sweet Grass Hills on left. Winters at Steering Wheel ranch on Old Man River. Boss **Dave Wells** (tall, thin Texan, drawl, "sho'"). Billy Gore, red-headed deputy. Wells leaves on horse-gathering trip with four men, returns with exhausted men; discharges four riders. Rock sees "doggies" with fresh Steering Wheel brand over possibly other brands, suspicious. Rock parts from remaining Texans under Sweet Grass Hills; heads for Fort Benton.

**Ch IV (A Dead Double):** Rock hired as mule packer by army civilian near Milk River (Fort Assiniboine 80 mi east); gets $25. Drops into Marias valley. Finds TL ranch, stable with bloody saddle on gray horse. Inside house: **Nona Parke** (~21, dark hair, gray eyes, imperious), **Betty** (3-4, blonde, blue eyes, rag doll, calls Rock "Doc"). Dead man: **Doc Martin** (brown hair, blue-rimmed bullet puncture in chest), who looks exactly like Rock. Doc was ambushed "up the river" while looking at cattle. Nona believes Elmer Duffy did it. Rock buries Doc beside Nona's father and mother (mother died at Betty's birth; father killed by horse fall). Half-breed girl **Mary Vieux** (16) nurse/helper.

**Ch V (Wrapped in Canvas):** Doc wrapped in canvas, buried at sunrise, 100 yards east under cottonwood in picket enclosure.

**Ch VI (Very Adroit Rock):** Nona hires Rock at $50/mo (Doc was $40); insists no sentiment. Explains Doc was jealous, quarreled with Elmer. Elmer rides up; Rock poses as Doc. Elmer threatened by "Doc" earlier; Rock reassures him ("I'm no bushwhacker"). Elmer: "I'll take you with an even break." Nona: "Adroit." Rock keeps impersonating for investigation.

**Ch VII (Mariners):** Rock rides TL range; meets Maltese Cross round-up at White Springs. **Charlie Shaw** (TL rider, ~20, blue eyes, slim, blond). **Alice Snell** (tawny yellow hair, black brows/lashes, deep blue eyes, dimple, green corduroy split skirt, carved saddle). Alice tells Rock to visit Nona; says Buck was at home ranch. **Buck Walters** (big, well-dressed, agate-gray eyes, high-crowned hat with silver band): glares at Rock, distaste for Doc. Nona says Alice "detests Buck," Buck is crazy about Alice. Rock and Nona ride range; uneasy about missing calves (60-80 short). Rock has feelings for Nona.

**Ch VIII (Getting Down to Cases):** Charlie warns: rumors Rock rustles with **Burris boys** behind the Goosebill (hill SW of Marias, halfway to Fort Benton). Buck's hard men: **Bill Hurley** and **Joe Stack** ("Killers"). Charlie says Buck wants Doc out of way over Alice. Rock shows Charlie the bloody saddle. Charlie: Doc was "a white man." Charlie knows more but withholds.

**Ch IX (Ordered South):** Rock rides to Fort Benton (one-time fur fort; Grand Union Hotel; ferry). Bar scene: Wells recognizes Rock Holloway; Buck says "Doc Martin." Rock hires two hay men. Night, Buck threatens: "This country ain't healthy for you no more... go South." Rock: "You go plumb to hell." Buck: "You'll get it." Buck: "I'll have you put away... inside of forty-eight hours." Buck says he has "a cinch" on the Maltese Cross and Alice.

**Ch X (Thirty Angry Men):** 24 hours later Alice gallops to Parke ranch: Buck and Elmer with 30 riders coming to hang Doc for rustling. Rock with carbine, cartridges; Nona and Alice on porch. Confrontation: Buck says "He is a thief." Nona calls it a lie. Rock declares he is Rock Holloway. Charlie slips inside, sides with Rock. Elmer: "If you ain't Doc Martin, there's only one other man you could be." Rock names Wells's identification. Elmer admits "Rock Holloway" (killed brother). Buck retracts, says Burrises incriminated Doc; "we cleaned out the Burrises." Alice: "You were afraid of him... I hate you!" Buck leaves.

**Ch XI (Riders on a Rise):** Nona's kiss-flirt talk: Rock says Nona "steals hearts." Nona: Alice to stay with her. Charlie reveals Burris cleanup. Rock and Charlie ride work horses; Charlie notices two riders on a rise. Ambush in ravine: Rock's horse shot; Rock fires back, kills one (**Hurley**). Rock chases second rider (**Stack**) on sorrel Maltese Cross horse; shoots horse out from under him, captures him, hog-ties him with hair macarte. Rock takes both horses.

**Ch XII (Stack Decides to Talk):** Rock's scalp grazed by bullet; he binds it with silk handkerchief/hat. Stack confesses Buck offered $500 each to Stack and Hurley to kill Rock. Rock burns Stack's foot to make him talk (Rock hates doing it). Stack admits Hurley shot Doc. Stack says Buck heading North with hand-picked crew. Rock lets Stack go on Maltese horse with blanket and grub.

**Ch XIII (On the Warpath):** Nona dresses wound (carbolic, court plaster). Rock says he's leaving; "I'm going on the warpath, but not the way you mean." Rock kisses Nona at Sangre's side; rides away. Reaches Capital K ranch (Kerr; Kerr knows Uncle Bill Sayre, who loaned him $20,000; Kerr offers men). Kerr warns Buck is dangerous.

**Ch XIV (Hot on the Trail):** Rock wires Sayre from Billings (long message; operator relays). Sayre's reply: "Act on your own judgment. Will back any action you take. Suspected this. Coming north, first train." Rock returns with a dozen Capital K men, chuck wagon, 100 horses. Ferry Fort Benton; ride to Marias above Nona's upper fence. Charlie Shaw joins, reveals he found hidden corrals on East Butte/Sweet Grass with branding chute; Buck and six hard men camped on creek 5 miles off; five riders with packs and 40 horses arrived from North.

**Ch XV (Popping Guns):** East Butte. Sweet Grass Hills: Gold Butte, West Butte, East Butte. Corrals dumbbell-shaped; branding fire; Buck and Dave Wells rebrand cattle (Maltese Cross to Steering Wheel). Lookout shoots Charlie (falls over bank, wounded). Rock fights, lures pursuers; his horse shot. Capital K men come. Buck charges on coal-black horse with white face; Rock shoots Buck at 20 yards; Buck dies. Black horse falls on Rock, breaks/injures leg; a bullet furrows under his armpit. Hurley and others killed; Wells dead.

**Ch XVI ("Certainly Not Sad"):** ~1,000 Maltese Cross steers with Steering Wheel brands, Capital K horses. Rock at Maltese Cross house with Uncle Bill. Rock explains plot: Buck borrowed $25,000 on coadministrator prospects, bought 1,200 Panhandle cattle; Rock showed brands transformed with marks on paper. Sayre offers Rock to run Maltese Cross; Rock undecided. Sayre: "Give the Parke girl credit." Sayre promises 100-200 calves for Nona. Elmer and Rock shake hands. Charlie wounded, sent to Benton. Rock to Nona: Nona says "I am glad that man is dead." Rock: "Do you like me?" Nona: "I like you a heap." Tears. "There are two times when every woman cries... when she's very happy. And I'm certainly not sad!"

---

## BOOK 2: THE RED DERELICT (Bertram Mitford, 1904 Methuen ed.)

**Principals:** **Wagram Gerard Wagram** (tall, dark, refined; heir to **Hilversea Court**, Bassingham area; chapel; "Priest's Walk" avenue ending in stone Calvary; martyred ancestor portrait in Spanish biretta; priest's hiding-hole in gallery). **Grantley Wagram, "the old Squire"** (~80, retired diplomat, iron-grey moustache). Wagram's elder brother died in motor accident. Half-brother **Everard Wagram** ("Butcher Ned"; wastrel; left ~10+ years earlier, felony; in Africa). Wagram's son **Gerard** (14, Hillside school; Rugby-minded; tutored by Churton). Wagram's first wife (took morphia). **Develin Hunt** (alias of **Jack Faro**, Kimberley adventurer; African trader; white beard; blackmailer; actual first husband of Wagram's mother).

**Calmours, Siege House, Bassingham:** **Major Calmour** (retired army vet, drunk, profane; dies of stroke). **Delia Calmour** (eldest, ~21+, handsome, hazel eyes, brunette, rounded, principled). **Clytie Calmour** (blue eyes, classical features, serene, scheming, typist, slangy). **Bob (Robert) Calmour** (raffish clerk for **Pownall and Skreet**, solicitors). Two younger brothers at school. Servant Emily.

**Haldanes, Fulkston:** **Haldane** (friend; ex-South Africa; magistrate; cynical, jolly). **Yvonne Haldane** ("Sunbeam"; tall golden-haired ~16; blue eyes; Angora cat **Poogie**). **Reggie Haldane** (son, school friend of Gerard). Father Gayle (family chaplain, Catholic priest, friend). **Monsignor Culham** (Squire's old friend, schoolfellow).

**Other:** Rundle (butler). Perrin (under-keeper), Hood (keeper), Bowles (village butcher), Thompson (groom), Briggs (gardener), Finlay. Smith (Golden Crown landlord, Bassingham). Charlie Vance ("Vance's eldest fool," breach of promise damages). Gee and Vincent (cycle makers), Warren (Bassingham cycle hire), Rowland Ward (taxidermy), Simcox and Yaxley (London solicitors), Father Sonnenbloem (German priest, Bassingham mission), Churton (rector-tutor). Mrs Pritchett, Pritchett (farm, Swanton road). Monsignor, Mrs Colville and daughter Lily (passengers). Captain Lawes (*Baleka*), Mr Ransome (4th officer), Gibson (chief officer, *Runic*), McAndrew (chief engineer, *Baleka*), Powis (chief officer, *Baleka*), Dr Foss (Bassingham).

**Bk2 Chapters:**
1. Brindled gnu (blue wildebeest) escapes west park; chases bicycle-riding Delia; bicycle destroyed; Wagram grips horns, is hurt (waistcoat ripped); Delia shoots gnu with his rabbit rifle. Delia's address: "Siege House, Bassingham." Wagram sends for Father Gayle chat ("Dead as a herring").
2. Afterwards: Wagram offers compensation; Warren hire.
3. Father and Son: Squire's history with Calmours (drunk, breach of promise). Half-brother Everard portrait; "bad lot"; left home in scandal, Australia; no news for years. Squire warns Wagram about Calmours. Squire expects Calmour lawsuit. "A Calmour at Hilversea! Pho!"
4. Siege House: Bob reads Delia's claim possibility; Clytie: "Capture the man."
5. Surprise visit: Wagram calls at Siege House; father drunk; Clytie typing, invites Wagram.
6. Solemnity: Corpus Christi procession; Delia assists; Yvonne; Haldane; Monsignor. Delia asks to attend chapel.
7. Derelict: newspaper item of *Rhodesian* passing derelict at 10°5'N 16°36'W (red hull, 900-1000 tons); Haldane recounts *Manchurian* near-collision.
8. Retribution: Bob insults Yvonne at Swanton gate; Wagram thrashes Bob with ground-ash. Mrs Pritchett's home-brew.
9. "We get no show": Clytie and Delia; Pownall and Skreet claim £1,000 for Delia (from Bob); Clytie gets typing commissions from Wagram.
10. At Haldane's: post-card albums; Delia wants Yvonne's companion post; Wagram cold on road.
11. Pownall & Skreet claims £1,000 from Squire (for Delia) and £1,000 from Wagram (for Bob). Squire refuses? Wagram sends £1,000 cheque to Delia; Delia tears it.
12. Bob punctures bicycles; Pownall's letter from Wagram refuses Bob's claim. Calmour father enraged.
13. Delia at Hilversea returns cheque; priest's hiding place; martyred relative (Wagram's ancestor, painted at Salamanca, left for St Omer).
14. Newspaper: *Carboceer* survivors; passenger **Develin Hunt** picked up; Squire recognizes name. "There can't be two Develin Hunts."
15. Delia's Hilversea illustrated article for *The Old Country Side*; Clytie's work; Delia's writing commission.
16. "A Calmour at Hilversea": Wagram gives Delia photographic commission; Delia asks about Catholicism; Father Sonnenbloem; choir practice; Arcadelt "Ave Maria."
17. Blackmail?: Develin Hunt visits Squire; claims Wagram's mother was his wife first; demands money; Squire rings for whisky.
18. Further counsels: Squire and Monsignor Culham; Culham advises demanding proof; Squire says he will not pay.
19. Interim—Peace: Delia plays organ at chapel; Haldane; grouse-shooting planned; Develin Hunt trespasses in park, Wagram turns him off politely.
20. A forced hand: Bob drunkenly insults Develin Hunt at Golden Crown; Hunt throws him out; Haldane nearly knocks Bob down; Hunt learns Haldane lives near.
21. The Bolt: Develin Hunt demands £25,000 (cheque) plus undertaking; Wagram overhears; learns he is not the son of the Squire; Hunt is his real father; the second marriage invalid.
22. "Nobody of Nowhere": Hunt gives Wagram the certificate; Everard location vague: Lourenço Marques, Swaziland; Hunt shakes Wagram's hand.
23. After the blow: Squire and Wagram; new will leaves personalty to Wagram; Wagram "Wagram Gerard, known as Wagram Gerard Wagram." Squire forbids Wagram to leave him. Wagram meets Delia and gipsy by the gate; Delia says the fortune: "battered ship," "green seas," "great happiness."
24. Requiem aeternam: Squire dies; funeral; Monsignor Culham sings requiem; Wagram, mourning. Delia takes up parish choir role.
25. The Red Derelict: *Baleka* (private steamer, Cape run); Mrs Colville and Lily; Wagram; derelict sighted near course; Ransome calls it "Red Derelict."
26. An omen: engines stop; Mrs Colville's fear; Captain Lawes; Wagram's cutting.
27. A sacrifice in vain: propeller shaft snaps; boats lowered; Lily left below; Wagram goes back below to find her; Captain forced into boat by crew; *Baleka* sinks; Lily found safe in boat.
28. The rusted pistol: Wagram in water; deck-chair saves him from shark; reaches derelict; finds rusted pistol with nameplate "E.W." (Everard's gift from Wagram). Derelict again.
29. Break-up at Bassingham: Delia's life empty; Calmour father dies of stroke; Delia's family moves to London; Haldane helps.
30. Concerning a terror: Wagram captive of cannibal tribe on coast; fed; sees human slaughter; hears of white renegade (Everard).
31. A dark place of the earth: Wagram explores forest; sees fetish-stone sacrifice; human skulls; a victim killed by unseen dart.
32. The open door: Everard (unnamed, scar round right eye) offers Wagram release for £15,000 cheque/agreement "Wagram Gerard Wagram"; Everard reacts with rage on learning name.
33. The closed door: Everard tears agreement; demands Gerard; Wagram defies; Wagram nearly beheaded/blood-cut.
34. The alternative: Everard orders Wagram tied to slaughter block; Wagram refuses to summon Gerard; spared temporarily.
35. Rout: freed by rescued native; attacks town; Everard's Maxim gun; Wagram flees into forest; alone with a native companion (the man he rescued).
36. On the great deep: Wagram escapes in canoe with native; native left behind; Wagram finds derelict again; retrieves tin case (marriage certificate of Develin Hunt's earlier marriage, four years prior to Wagram's mother's wedding); canoe sinks; left alone on derelict.
37. The echo of a prophecy: Delia on *Runic* forces captain to stop (she saw man on derelict); *Runic* rescues Wagram; Gibson; Delia's voyage happiness.
38. Time's chance: Wagram home at Hilversea; examines tin case; marriage certificate shows Develin Hunt's first wife (alive); need to trace South Africa. Wagram thinks of Delia.
39. Time's consummation: Gerard, Yvonne (hair up); *Bassingham Chronicle* reports Develin Hunt knocked down by motor car, dying at Golden Crown. Wagram and Haldane visit. Hunt is Jack Faro, Haldane's old Kimberley comrade; Hunt says Everard = "Butcher Ned" and Wagram's pistol bore Everard's bullet. Wagram forgives Hunt, shakes hands. Hunt dies that night.
40. Conclusion: Wagram proposes to Delia at Hilversea; she accepts. Note: Red Derelict never sighted again; collision with *Runic* possibly sank her.
